task_1.title: Expose xarray.indexes as a public index API namespace
task_1.description: The 2025.7.0 update makes index APIs easier to discover and rely on by exposing the indexes namespace from top-level xarray and publishing RangeIndex and CoordinateTransformIndex there as public imports, along with the related CoordinateTransform symbol.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray provides a stable public indexes namespace so users can access documented index classes through xarray.indexes, including RangeIndex and CoordinateTransformIndex, without relying on private or indirect imports.

expectation.grounded: The package should expose the `indexes` namespace on the top-level `xarray` module and treat `xarray.indexes` as a public API surface. `RangeIndex` and `CoordinateTransformIndex` should be publicly importable from `xarray.indexes`, and the namespace should continue to expose the existing index types while also making `CoordinateTransform` available from that namespace.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to discover and import the supported index-related classes from a single public `xarray.indexes` namespace, including through `xarray.indexes` after importing xarray.

constraints.grounded: Adding the public namespace exposure must not remove or rename the existing public index exports from `xarray.indexes`. The change should extend the public API surface by exposing additional supported symbols and the namespace itself, without altering the meaning of existing index classes.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden access to index APIs without breaking existing imports or changing the behavior of already supported index classes.

behavior: Importing `xarray` should expose an `indexes` namespace as part of the top-level public module surface.
`RangeIndex` is a supported public export of `xarray.indexes`.
`CoordinateTransformIndex` is a supported public export of `xarray.indexes`.
`CoordinateTransform` becomes available from `xarray.indexes` alongside the existing index-related public symbols.
Previously exposed index classes in `xarray.indexes`, such as `Index`, `PandasIndex`, and `PandasMultiIndex`, remain publicly available.
acceptance_criteria: When a user imports `xarray as xr`, `xr.indexes` should be available as a public namespace.
When a user imports `RangeIndex` from `xarray.indexes`, the import should succeed through the documented public API.
When a user imports `CoordinateTransformIndex` from `xarray.indexes`, the import should succeed through the documented public API.
When a user imports existing index classes from `xarray.indexes`, those imports should continue to succeed after the upgrade.
When a user looks for index-related public APIs, the supported classes should be discoverable from the `xarray.indexes` namespace rather than requiring internal import paths.

task_3.title: Improve context on write-time encoding failures
task_3.description: The update improves diagnostics when dataset data or metadata cannot be encoded for disk writes. Encoding failures now surface which variable or attribute caused the error, making write failures easier to debug without changing successful serialization behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that write operations clearly identify the variable or attribute responsible when encoding data for disk fails, so users can diagnose invalid values or metadata during serialization.

expectation.grounded: When write paths such as Dataset.to_netcdf() run backend or CF encoding and an encoder raises, the original exception should be re-raised with supplemental note context naming the offending variable or attribute and including its value representation. This contextual annotation should apply consistently to variable encoding in AbstractWritableDataStore.encode(), WritableCFDataStore.encode(), and cf_encoder(), and to attribute encoding in backend datastore encoding.
expectation.conceptual: If saving a dataset fails during encoding, the error should make clear which variable or attribute triggered the failure while preserving the underlying error type and reason.

constraints.grounded: Successful writes and encoded results must remain unchanged. The encoder must not replace or mask the original exception class or core failure reason; it should only add contextual diagnostics. Variable-context reporting must no longer depend on lower-level encoders receiving a separate name argument in order to identify the failing variable.
constraints.conceptual: Do not alter normal serialization behavior or hide the original error. Only improve failure diagnostics, and do so consistently across write-time encoding paths.

behavior: A failure while encoding an individual variable for output now carries supplemental context identifying that variable and its current value representation.
A failure while encoding an output attribute now carries supplemental context identifying that attribute and its current value representation.
Failures raised during CF variable encoding are annotated with the same variable-specific context before propagating upward.
Writable CF datastore encoding uses the shared encoding flow so variable and attribute failures receive the same contextual diagnostics after any required dtype normalization.
acceptance_criteria: When saving a dataset fails because a variable cannot be encoded for the selected storage format, the operation should raise the original encoding error and include additional context that identifies the variable responsible.

When saving a dataset fails because an attribute value cannot be encoded, the operation should raise the original encoding error and include additional context that identifies the attribute responsible.
When the failure originates during CF encoding before backend serialization completes, the surfaced error should still identify the offending variable.
When all variables and attributes are encodable, serialization behavior and produced output should be unchanged from prior releases.

task_2.title: Honor Zarr store consolidated metadata support
task_2.description: The Zarr integration now recognizes a Zarr v3 store capability flag for consolidated metadata support. Stores that explicitly opt out of consolidated metadata should be handled in non-consolidated mode automatically, while older stores that do not expose the flag must continue to behave as before.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Zarr v3 stores which explicitly do not support consolidated metadata can still be opened and used without attempting unsupported consolidated-metadata behavior.

expectation.grounded: For Zarr v3 backends, xarray should inspect the store attribute `supports_consolidated_metadata` during Zarr open-parameter resolution. When that attribute is present and false, `xarray.open_zarr` and related Zarr backend operations should behave as though consolidated metadata handling is disabled, including disabling close-time metadata consolidation. Stores that do not expose the attribute should continue to be treated as supporting consolidated metadata.
expectation.conceptual: If a Zarr store advertises that consolidated metadata is unsupported, the library should automatically use normal non-consolidated metadata behavior instead of attempting a consolidated path. Existing behavior should stay the same for stores that support consolidated metadata or do not declare otherwise.

constraints.grounded: This capability check should only affect Zarr v3 stores. It must not change behavior for stores whose `supports_consolidated_metadata` attribute is missing or truthy, and it must preserve prior consolidated-metadata behavior for those stores.
constraints.conceptual: Only stores that explicitly opt out of consolidated metadata should see changed behavior. Older or fully supported stores must remain backward compatible.

behavior: When a Zarr v3 store exposes `supports_consolidated_metadata=false`, xarray should skip consolidated metadata mode even if consolidated handling would otherwise be attempted by default.
When that same store is written or closed through the Zarr backend, xarray should not request metadata consolidation on close.
When a store does not define `supports_consolidated_metadata`, xarray should continue using the pre-existing consolidated metadata behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Zarr v3 store with `supports_consolidated_metadata=false`, when it is opened through `xarray.open_zarr`, then xarray should use non-consolidated metadata handling rather than trying consolidated metadata first.

Given a Zarr v3 store with `supports_consolidated_metadata=false`, when xarray performs a backend write flow that would otherwise consolidate metadata on close, then no consolidated-metadata close action should be requested.
Given a Zarr store that does not expose `supports_consolidated_metadata`, when it is opened or written through the Zarr backend, then behavior should remain consistent with earlier versions.

task_5.title: Pydap NumPy 2.3 compatibility note has no production runtime change
task_5.description: The 2025.7.0 release note references Pydap comparison handling around NumPy 2.3.0, but the provided production code diff is empty. Based on the supplied evidence, this item represents test and validation alignment rather than a shipped library behavior change, so upgrading from 2025.6.1 to 2025.7.0 does not introduce a new runtime requirement for users for this item.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from 2025.6.1 to 2025.7.0 does not require application changes for this release-note item, because the provided evidence indicates compatibility validation around NumPy 2.3.0 without a corresponding production behavior change.

expectation.grounded: For this release-note entry, the supplied `2025.7.0` production diff does not show any public API, backend logic, warning, exception, or return-value change. Users upgrading should therefore observe no new runtime behavior attributable to this item in Pydap-backed xarray usage.
expectation.conceptual: This upgrade item should be treated as a non-runtime compatibility note. Applications using the library should continue to behave the same after upgrading, with no new feature adoption or code migration required for this specific change.

constraints.grounded: Do not describe or require changes to tests, test fixtures, or test-only expectations. Do not claim new runtime guarantees beyond what is supported by the release note and the absence of production code changes in the provided diff.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the requirement limited to observable user impact. It should not introduce implementation steps, internal details, or obligations that are unsupported by shipped runtime changes.

behavior: No production code changes are evidenced for this release-note item in the provided diff.
No new public API surface, warning behavior, exception behavior, or documented runtime migration requirement is introduced for users by this item.
The item is best understood as compatibility validation related to NumPy 2.3.0 rather than a shipped feature or fix that changes application behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user upgrades from 2025.6.1 to 2025.7.0, this release-note item should not require code changes in application logic.

When using existing Pydap-backed workflows after the upgrade, users should not encounter a new public API, new warning, new exception contract, or changed observable runtime behavior attributable to this item.
Release communication for this item should describe it as non-runtime upgrade information rather than a user-facing behavioral change.

task_4.title: Require Python 3.11+ and newer dependency floors
task_4.description: Version 2025.7.0 raises the minimum supported Python version to 3.11 and increases the minimum supported versions of core dependencies and integrations. The release also aligns runtime behavior with Python 3.11 standard-library features, including native exception notes, so older environments are no longer part of the supported contract.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2025.7.0 is treated as an environment compatibility change: the library should only be expected to run on Python 3.11 or newer and with the newer minimum supported dependency versions, while preserving normal behavior for users on supported environments.

expectation.grounded: The supported runtime floor is Python 3.11 or newer. Minimum supported dependency versions are raised, including array-api-strict 1.1, boto3 1.34, bottleneck 1.4, cartopy 0.23, dask-core 2024.6, distributed 2024.6, flox 0.9, h5py 3.11, hdf5 1.14, iris 3.9, lxml 5.1, matplotlib-base 3.8, numba 0.60, numbagg 0.8, numpy 1.26, packaging 24.1, pandas 2.2, pint 0.24, pydap 3.5, scipy 1.13, sparse 0.15, and zarr 2.18. On supported runtimes, Python 3.11 standard-library typing features such as Self and TypeAlias are assumed, typing_extensions is no longer required for that compatibility, and contextual exceptions should surface notes through BaseException.add_note.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to 2025.7.0 must move to a newer baseline environment. The release should behave as a support-matrix update rather than a feature redesign: existing workflows continue on supported setups, but the runtime and dependency stack must satisfy the new minimums and contextual errors should use normal Python 3.11 exception notes.

constraints.grounded: Do not claim support for Python 3.10 or dependency versions below the published floors. Preserve existing observable behavior of supported APIs aside from the narrowed environment support and the use of native Python 3.11 exception notes for contextual failures. The supported contract must not rely on typing_extensions for Self or TypeAlias.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only narrow which environments are supported. It should not otherwise alter successful user workflows on supported installations, and it should not require legacy compatibility layers that were only needed for older Python versions.

behavior: Importing and running the library now assumes Python 3.11+ standard-library typing support instead of fallback compatibility shims for older Python versions.
Failures that attach contextual path or mapping information should expose that context as standard Python exception notes on supported runtimes.
Supported installations now require the raised minimum versions of the runtime and listed dependencies; environments below those floors are outside the supported behavior contract.
acceptance_criteria: When the library is installed on Python 3.11 or newer with dependency versions at or above the published minimums, supported user workflows should run without requiring typing_extensions-based compatibility for standard typing features.
When an operation adds contextual information to an exception on a supported runtime, the resulting exception should carry that context as a standard Python exception note.
When users assess upgrade readiness, the documented compatibility contract should clearly exclude Python 3.10 and dependency versions below the new minimum floors.

task_6.title: Fix SciPy netCDF3 subset writes after lazy decoding
task_6.description: The SciPy-backed netCDF3 read path now preserves lazy indexing for decoded arrays so datasets loaded from disk can be subsetted, transposed, and written back without failing. This removes a serialization error on selected data and aligns decoded string, boolean, and endian-converted variables with the lazy behavior of other backends.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that datasets opened from netCDF3 files through the SciPy backend can be subsetted and written back to NetCDF without failing, including cases where variables undergo CF decoding such as stacked byte strings, booleans, native-endian conversion, or other elementwise decoding.

expectation.grounded: Variables returned by the SciPy backend through `xr.open_dataset` should behave like other backend-backed variables by remaining lazily indexable after CF decoding. After `Dataset.sel`, `Dataset.isel`, transpose, or mixed scalar, slice, and vector indexing, decoded arrays such as `StackedBytesArray`, `BoolTypeArray`, `NativeEndiannessArray`, and other `_ElementwiseFunctionArray` wrappers should continue to support downstream lazy indexing and `Dataset.to_netcdf` should no longer fail with `AttributeError` caused by missing outer or vectorized indexing support on the SciPy backend array wrapper.
expectation.conceptual: Opening a netCDF3 dataset with the SciPy engine, selecting a subset, and saving that subset back to NetCDF should succeed. Decoded values should stay lazily subsettable through common indexing and transpose operations instead of breaking when the data is later materialized or serialized.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing decoded value semantics while changing the indexing behavior: materialized string, boolean, and endian-normalized data should keep their expected decoded dtypes and values; explicit indexing adapters and existing duck arrays should not acquire redundant lazy wrappers; and decoded arrays should remain compatible with outer indexing, vectorized indexing, and transpose before materialization.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the decoded results the same while making chained read-select-write workflows safe. The fix should improve lazy behavior without changing the user-visible meaning of decoded data or requiring callers to eagerly load arrays first.

behavior: The SciPy netCDF3 backend now exposes opened variables through a lazy indexing layer, so backend-backed arrays support downstream outer and vectorized indexing during later operations.

Decoded string, boolean, and native-endian arrays keep their decoding wrapper after indexing instead of immediately materializing to a NumPy array, so lazy indexing can continue across chained selections.
Elementwise-decoded arrays preserve lazy behavior across transpose as well as indexing, allowing re-ordered decoded data to be materialized or serialized later without losing decoding semantics.
CF decoding only adds lazy indexing for bare non-duck backend arrays and does not redundantly wrap arrays that are already duck arrays or explicit indexing adapters.
Variables returned from the in-memory store are copied and surfaced as lazily indexed data, aligning their indexing behavior with backend-loaded variables during later serialization.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset is opened from a netCDF3 file with the SciPy engine and a subset is taken with label-based or positional indexing, calling `to_netcdf` on the subset should complete without raising `AttributeError` related to backend indexing.

When decoded string data from a SciPy-opened dataset is sliced, indexed with arrays, or reduced to scalars before writing, the selected values should serialize successfully and preserve the same decoded content.
When decoded boolean or native-endian variables are indexed and then materialized or written out, they should retain their expected decoded dtypes and values.
When a decoded variable is transposed before later access or serialization, it should remain usable without forcing premature eager conversion or breaking subsequent indexing.

When CF decoding receives data that is already a duck array or already provides explicit lazy indexing, the externally observable indexing behavior should remain stable rather than changing because of duplicate wrapping.

task_7.title: Auto-correct stale character dimension names for netCDF string writes
task_7.description: Version 2025.7.0 fixes netCDF serialization for string variables that were loaded from character arrays and later subsetted or otherwise reduced in width. When persisted string-dimension metadata no longer matches the actual encoded string length, the library now corrects the character-dimension name, emits a user-visible warning when a mismatch is detected, and proceeds with writing instead of failing due to dimension-length clashes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that writing datasets with fixed-width string variables back to netCDF still succeeds after subsetting or other shape changes, even when saved character-dimension metadata is stale. Ensure that inconsistent string-dimension metadata is corrected automatically and surfaced to users with a warning instead of causing serialization failures.

expectation.grounded: When string variables are encoded for netCDF via `Dataset.to_netcdf()` / `DataArray.to_netcdf()`, `CharacterArrayCoder` must validate any existing `encoding['char_dim_name']` against the actual encoded string length. If the supplied name ends with a numeric suffix and that suffix does not match the current string length, the encoder must retain the textual prefix, replace the suffix with the actual length, and emit a user-level warning identifying the affected variable. If `char_dim_name` has no numeric suffix but `encoding['original_shape'][-1]` disagrees with the current string length, the encoder must derive a disambiguated character-dimension name by appending the actual length and emit a user-level warning. In either mismatch case, netCDF serialization must continue using the corrected character-dimension name rather than failing because stale metadata reuses an incompatible dimension.
expectation.conceptual: Saving a dataset containing string data back to netCDF should automatically reconcile outdated character-dimension metadata with the string width that is actually being written. If the library has to correct an inconsistent string-dimension name, it should warn the user and still produce a valid netCDF result instead of failing with a shape or broadcasting error.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for string encodings whose `char_dim_name` already matches the actual encoded length. When no custom `char_dim_name` is provided, continue generating the default `string{length}` character dimension name from the current string width. Limit the correction logic to byte-string-to-character-array netCDF encoding paths, and preserve applicability across both netCDF3 and netCDF4 variable encoding flows.
constraints.conceptual: Only intervene when stored string-dimension metadata is inconsistent with the data being written. Already-correct string encodings should behave as before, and ordinary netCDF writes without custom string-dimension metadata should remain unaffected.

behavior: If a string variable carries a `char_dim_name` whose trailing numeric length does not match the actual encoded string width, the write path replaces that numeric suffix with the actual width before creating the character-array dimension.

If a string variable carries a `char_dim_name` without a numeric suffix but its saved `original_shape` indicates a different final string length than the current data, the write path appends the actual width to the provided base name before writing.
When either kind of mismatch is corrected, the library emits a user-visible warning that identifies the affected variable and indicates that a corrected character-dimension name is being used.
When no `char_dim_name` is provided, the generated character dimension continues to use the default naming pattern based on the actual string width.
The corrected naming and warning behavior applies when variables are encoded through both netCDF3 and netCDF4 serialization paths.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset loaded from netCDF contains fixed-width string variables and a subset reduces one variable's string width, calling `to_netcdf()` should still succeed even if the variable retains stale `char_dim_name` metadata from the original file.

When a provided `char_dim_name` ends in a number that does not match the string width being written, serialization should use the same base name with the actual width and issue a warning rather than failing.

When a provided `char_dim_name` has no numeric suffix but the saved original string length conflicts with the current width, serialization should derive a width-qualified character-dimension name, warn, and continue.
When `char_dim_name` already matches the actual width, writing should proceed without mismatch warnings and without altering the intended dimension name.
When no custom string-dimension name is supplied, writing should continue to use the default generated name based on the actual width.

task_8.title: Fix DataTree assert_equal mismatch reporting
task_8.description: Upgrade DataTree equality assertions so mismatched DataTree objects produce the intended comparison failure details instead of crashing with an internal ambiguous-truth-value ValueError. This restores usable user-facing error reporting for xarray.testing.assert_equal on unequal DataTree inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that comparing two different DataTree objects with xarray.testing.assert_equal reports a normal DataTree equality failure with useful mismatch details instead of crashing with an internal ValueError.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.testing.assert_equal() is given two DataTree instances that are not equal, the comparison must preserve the assert_equal compatibility mode through DataTree dataset diff generation so mismatches are reported as the intended comparison failure. The failure output should identify the affected DataTree node and include the dataset-level difference summary, and the comparison must not raise the ambiguous truth-value ValueError seen in 2025.6.1.
expectation.conceptual: DataTree equality assertions should fail cleanly and informatively. If two DataTree objects differ, users should get a readable explanation of where the difference is and what differs, not an unrelated internal exception.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the meaning of successful DataTree equality checks or the compatibility semantics used by xarray.testing.assert_equal. The fix should be limited to mismatch reporting for unequal DataTree objects and should preserve node-wise comparison behavior while preventing unrelated runtime exceptions during diff construction.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing equality behavior intact for matching objects and for normal comparison semantics. The change should only make unequal DataTree comparisons fail in the expected, user-readable way.

behavior: xarray.testing.assert_equal() now carries the correct equality compatibility semantics through DataTree mismatch formatting instead of converting them to a form that can trigger invalid array truth-value evaluation.
If corresponding DataTree nodes contain unequal datasets, the reported comparison failure identifies the mismatching node and includes a dataset difference summary for that node.
Unequal DataTree comparisons no longer abort with the ambiguous-truth-value ValueError that previously appeared when dataset differences involved array-valued comparison results.
acceptance_criteria: When xarray.testing.assert_equal() compares two equal DataTree objects, it should continue to complete without raising.
When xarray.testing.assert_equal() compares two different DataTree objects, it should fail with the normal assertion-style comparison failure used by the API instead of raising ValueError.
When the mismatch is inside a named or nested DataTree node, the reported failure should identify that node in the mismatch output.

When unequal node datasets differ in structural or array-backed properties such as dimensions or variable layout, mismatch reporting should still complete and provide a readable dataset-level summary.

task_9.title: Honor check_dim_order=False for DataTree equality assertions
task_9.description: xarray 2025.7.0 fixes a bug where DataTree equality assertions ignored the opt-out for dimension-order checking. After the update, equivalent DataTree contents that differ only by dimension order can be treated as equal when users disable dimension-order enforcement, while real mismatches still fail.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.testing.assert_equal treats DataTree inputs consistently with other xarray objects when check_dim_order is disabled, so DataTree comparisons do not fail solely because corresponding datasets use a different dimension order.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.testing.assert_equal compares two DataTree objects with check_dim_order=False, it should apply the same dimension-order normalization used for Variable, DataArray, and Dataset comparisons to the datasets contained in corresponding tree nodes before evaluating equality. If compared node datasets do not expose the same set of dimension names, or if the DataTree objects differ in data or structure for reasons other than order alone, the comparison should continue to fail with the normal assertion behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Ignoring dimension order should also work for DataTree equality checks. If two DataTree objects are otherwise equivalent and differ only in axis ordering within matching nodes, equality comparison should succeed when dimension-order checking is turned off, but genuine content or structure differences should still be reported.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the default strict behavior when check_dim_order=True. Only ignore pure dimension-order differences, and only where the compared datasets share the same dimensions in a different order. Preserve existing comparison behavior for non-DataTree xarray objects and for mismatches that are not reducible to ordering alone.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped: opting out of dimension-order checking may relax order-only differences, but it must not hide real incompatibilities or alter normal strict comparisons unless the caller explicitly requests it.

behavior: xarray.testing.assert_equal should honor check_dim_order=False when both inputs are DataTree objects instead of ignoring that flag.
For corresponding datasets inside a DataTree comparison, dimension order should be normalized before equality is checked when the only difference is ordering.
If the compared datasets do not have the same dimensions, the comparison should not coerce them into alignment and should still fail through normal assertion semantics.
When check_dim_order=True, DataTree equality checks should remain order-sensitive.
acceptance_criteria: When two DataTree objects contain matching node datasets with identical values and metadata but different dimension order, xarray.testing.assert_equal should fail by default and succeed when called with check_dim_order=False.
When two DataTree objects differ by dimension names, missing dimensions, unequal values, or unequal tree structure, xarray.testing.assert_equal with check_dim_order=False should still fail.
When comparing Variable, DataArray, or Dataset inputs, the upgrade should preserve the existing check_dim_order behavior.

task_10.title: Clarify Pydap string dtype compatibility as non-breaking
task_10.description: The provided 2025.7.0 upgrade evidence does not show a production code change. The release note indicates that Pydap backend validation was updated to treat string arrays as NumPy byte-string dtype `S`, reflecting dependency behavior around Pydap string conversion rather than a new user-facing API, feature, or breaking runtime change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from 2025.6.1 to 2025.7.0 does not require user code changes for Pydap-backed string data handling, and that the release is treated as compatibility maintenance rather than a new runtime feature or breaking change.

expectation.grounded: Based on the provided artifacts, no production-code change is present for xarray's public Pydap-facing APIs such as opening datasets through the Pydap backend. The release note only establishes that Pydap string arrays should be considered compatible with NumPy byte-string dtype `S` handling in backend validation, including environments where Pydap may otherwise yield unicode arrays.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should not need to adopt a new API or migration path. Pydap-backed string data should remain interoperable across supported dependency versions, with byte-string versus unicode representation differences treated as backend compatibility details rather than a user-facing behavioral change.

constraints.grounded: Do not infer a new public API, configuration option, warning, exception type, or changed calling pattern from this update. Preserve existing Pydap backend usage and treat the change as non-breaking because the provided production diff contains no runtime modifications.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the upgrade transparent for existing applications. The change should not introduce new knobs, new failure modes, or required rewrites for consumers already using the Pydap backend.

behavior: No production runtime behavior change is evidenced in the provided code diff for the 2025.7.0 update.
No new public API surface, user-visible warning, or documented exception behavior is introduced by the provided upgrade artifacts.

The release note indicates backend compatibility normalization around Pydap string arrays being treated consistently with NumPy byte-string dtype `S`, but this is evidenced as validation maintenance rather than a shipped runtime feature change.
acceptance_criteria: When upgrading from 2025.6.1 to 2025.7.0, applications using the Pydap backend should not need to change their `open_dataset(..., engine='pydap')` usage solely because of this update.
The upgrade should not require users to adopt a new public option, API, or error-handling path for Pydap string-array compatibility.
Consumers should be able to treat the Pydap string dtype note in 2025.7.0 as non-breaking compatibility maintenance rather than a new observable product feature.

task_11.title: Restore reliable timedelta64 disk decoding
task_11.description: xarray 2025.7.0 fixes a regression in 2025.6.1 where encoded numpy.timedelta64 values carrying a serialized dtype could fail to decode when reopened from disk. The update makes dtype-based timedelta decoding consume dtype metadata safely, use the serialized dtype resolution by default, honor explicit CFTimedeltaCoder time_unit overrides, and warn while coercing unsupported resolutions to pandas-supported units.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that datasets and variables containing encoded numpy.timedelta64 values can be reopened and decoded without manual removal of a serialized dtype attribute, and ensure that decoded timedelta resolution follows the stored dtype by default unless the caller explicitly requests a different time unit.

expectation.grounded: When xarray.open_dataset() or CF timedelta decoding processes an encoded timedelta variable with a serialized dtype attribute, CFTimedeltaCoder should consume that dtype metadata during decode instead of triggering a dtype-overwrite failure. With CFTimedeltaCoder(time_unit=None), dtype-based decoding should derive the output timedelta64 resolution from the serialized dtype; with an explicit CFTimedeltaCoder(time_unit=...), that requested resolution should take precedence. Encoded resolutions outside pandas-supported timedelta64 units should emit a user-visible warning and decode using 's' for coarser resolutions or 'ns' for finer resolutions.
expectation.conceptual: Opening data files that contain encoded timedeltas should succeed without manual metadata cleanup. By default, decoded timedeltas should use the resolution described by the stored data, while an explicitly requested decode resolution should override that default. If stored timedelta precision is outside the supported range, decoding should still proceed with a warning and a compatible fallback resolution.

constraints.grounded: Do not require users to strip a serialized dtype attribute before decoding. Preserve units-based timedelta decoding when dtype-driven decoding is not used, defaulting to nanosecond resolution only when no explicit time_unit is provided and no dtype-derived resolution is being applied. If a timedelta dtype attribute is present but decoding proceeds via the units path, remove that conflicting dtype metadata during decode so later round-tripping does not fail because of duplicated dtype state.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must remove the regression without introducing new metadata conflicts or unpredictable dtype changes. Existing timedelta decoding modes should continue to work, explicit caller overrides must remain authoritative, and unsupported stored resolutions should degrade predictably instead of causing hard failures.

behavior: Reopening encoded timedelta data from disk no longer fails with a dtype attribute overwrite error when the variable carries serialized timedelta dtype metadata.
For dtype-encoded timedeltas, the default CFTimedeltaCoder behavior now uses the serialized dtype to choose the decoded timedelta64 resolution instead of always forcing nanosecond resolution.
An explicit CFTimedeltaCoder(time_unit=...) override takes precedence over the serialized dtype when decoding dtype-encoded timedeltas.
If the serialized timedelta resolution is coarser than seconds, decoding emits a user-visible warning and coerces the result to timedelta64[s].
If the serialized timedelta resolution is finer than nanoseconds, decoding emits a user-visible warning and coerces the result to timedelta64[ns].

When decoding falls back to the units-based path while serialized timedelta dtype metadata is present, that dtype metadata is removed during decode so decoded data can be re-encoded without conflicting dtype state.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dataset written with encoded numpy.timedelta64 data that includes serialized dtype metadata, when it is reopened with xarray.open_dataset(), then decoding should succeed without requiring the user to delete dtype metadata manually.

Given encoded timedelta data with serialized dtype metadata using a supported resolution such as s, ms, us, or ns, when it is decoded with the default CFTimedeltaCoder configuration, then the resulting variable should use the same timedelta64 resolution indicated by the serialized dtype.

Given encoded timedelta data with serialized dtype metadata, when decoding is configured with an explicit CFTimedeltaCoder(time_unit=...) value, then the decoded timedelta64 resolution should follow the explicit time_unit rather than the serialized dtype.

Given encoded timedelta data whose serialized dtype resolution is coarser than seconds or finer than nanoseconds, when it is decoded, then decoding should complete with a user-visible warning and the result should use the nearest supported boundary resolution of seconds or nanoseconds respectively.

Given encoded timedelta data that is decoded through the units-based path while serialized timedelta dtype metadata is present, when the decoded result is later re-encoded, then the decode step should not have preserved conflicting dtype metadata that would cause a round-trip failure.

task_12.title: Fix timedelta64 CF encoding for 32-bit backends
task_12.description: Timedelta CF serialization now preserves the original timedelta resolution in metadata while using units-based storage selection, preventing false write failures on 32-bit-only formats and making default decoding honor the stored resolution unless a caller explicitly overrides it.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `numpy.timedelta64` data can be written and read through CF/netCDF encoding without spurious cast failures on formats limited to 32-bit integers, while preserving the original timedelta resolution in encoded metadata and decoding to that stored resolution by default.

expectation.grounded: When `numpy.timedelta64` variables are encoded for CF-compatible storage, the encoded representation should always include a `dtype` attribute matching the in-memory timedelta resolution and a `units` attribute describing the serialized unit. Default encoding should use the units-based timedelta serialization path so that backends limited to 32-bit integer storage can write compatible values when they fit, including cases where `timedelta64[ns]` values can be represented in coarser units. Automatic masking metadata must not introduce an incompatible `int64` `_FillValue` that makes an otherwise valid `int32` encoding fail. `CFTimedeltaCoder` should default `time_unit` to `None`, decode to the resolution recorded by the stored timedelta `dtype` when no override is supplied, and still let an explicit `time_unit` take precedence. If dtype-based decoding is disabled while units-based decoding remains enabled, conflicting stored timedelta `dtype` metadata should not block a successful round trip.
expectation.conceptual: Timedelta values should round-trip through file storage predictably. Writing them to older or more limited formats should succeed whenever the serialized values fit the target storage type, stored metadata should preserve the original timedelta precision, and decoding should either respect that stored precision or use an explicitly requested output precision.

constraints.grounded: Preserve support for explicit output `units`, explicit non-timedelta storage dtypes, and packed timedelta encodings that use `add_offset` or `scale_factor`. Do not regress successful round-tripping of encoded timedeltas, and do not leave metadata combinations that cause re-encoding errors after decoding. Continue representing encoded timedeltas with observable CF metadata rather than silently dropping `dtype` or `units` information.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should not take away existing ways to control serialized units, storage type, packing, or decode resolution. It must avoid introducing metadata or defaults that turn a successful write/read cycle into a failure or a silent change in meaning.

behavior: Encoding `numpy.timedelta64` data now always records the original timedelta resolution in a `dtype` attribute alongside the serialized `units`.

Default timedelta encoding uses a units-based representation instead of forcing literal `int64` nanosecond storage, allowing 32-bit-only formats such as netCDF3 to store compatible timedeltas when their serialized values fit.
Automatic encoding no longer relies on a default `int64` `_FillValue` that can trigger a false `int64` to `int32` coercion error during write.
Timedelta variables encoded with packing metadata such as `add_offset` or `scale_factor` continue through the supported units-based path instead of being rejected by the default encoding mode.
Decoding with `CFTimedeltaCoder` now defaults to preserving the stored timedelta resolution when `time_unit` is not provided, rather than always decoding to nanoseconds.
Providing an explicit `time_unit` during decode still overrides the stored timedelta resolution.
When decoding relies on units but not dtype-based decoding, conflicting stored timedelta `dtype` metadata is cleared so the decoded variable can be re-encoded successfully.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset containing `numpy.timedelta64` values is written to a backend that only supports 32-bit integer storage, the write should succeed if the chosen serialized units make the values representable in that storage type.
When a timedelta variable is encoded without a caller-supplied decode override, the stored metadata should expose both the original timedelta `dtype` and the serialized `units`.
When a caller requests a specific storage dtype such as `int32`, the on-disk numeric type should follow that request without failing because of an automatically chosen `int64` fill value.
When timedeltas are encoded with packing parameters such as `add_offset` or `scale_factor`, encoding should still complete through the supported timedelta serialization behavior.
When stored timedelta data is decoded with default `CFTimedeltaCoder` behavior, the resulting timedelta dtype should match the resolution recorded in the stored metadata.
When the same stored timedelta data is decoded with an explicit `CFTimedeltaCoder(time_unit=...)`, the resulting dtype should use the caller-requested resolution instead of the stored one.
When dtype-based timedelta decoding is disabled but units-based decoding remains enabled, decoding and re-encoding the data should not fail because of leftover conflicting timedelta dtype metadata.

task_13.title: Propagate variable names through backend string encoding
task_13.description: Writable datastore backends now preserve optional variable-name context while encoding variables for output and forward that context into NetCDF and Zarr string encoders. This improves user-visible diagnostics for string and char-array serialization issues and adds clearer context when variable or attribute encoding fails.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that writable backends preserve per-variable context while encoding variables for output, especially for string and char-array serialization, so backend warnings or failures identify the affected variable and char-array dimension-name handling remains associated with the correct variable.

expectation.grounded: `AbstractWritableDataStore.encode_variable` must accept an optional `name` argument, and writable backend overrides in `NetCDF4DataStore`, `H5NetCDFStore`, `ScipyDataStore`, and `ZarrStore` must preserve that signature and forward `name` into backend encoders such as `encode_nc3_variable`, `_encode_nc4_variable`, and `encode_zarr_variable`. NetCDF string encoding must forward `name` into `EncodedStringCoder.encode` and `CharacterArrayCoder.encode`. When `AbstractWritableDataStore.encode` encounters an exception from `encode_variable` or `encode_attribute`, it should re-raise the original exception with an added note identifying the variable or attribute key and the value being encoded.
expectation.conceptual: When xarray encodes variables for storage, string-related encoding should keep track of which variable is being processed so any char-array or string warnings and errors point to the right variable. Serialization failures should also report which variable or attribute caused the problem without changing the underlying failure type.

constraints.grounded: `encode_variable` must remain callable without a provided `name`. Existing encoding behavior for non-string data and existing backend-specific return values should remain unchanged aside from the added name propagation and exception notes.
constraints.conceptual: Normal serialization behavior should stay the same for unaffected data. The change should add context and robustness without requiring callers to change ordinary save workflows or altering unrelated encoding results.

behavior: `AbstractWritableDataStore.encode_variable` and affected backend overrides now accept `name=None`.
NetCDF3, NetCDF4, H5NetCDF, Scipy, and Zarr writable backends forward variable-name context into their lower-level variable encoders.
NetCDF string encoding passes the variable name through `EncodedStringCoder` and `CharacterArrayCoder`, allowing string and char-array encoding logic to operate with per-variable context.
Exceptions raised while encoding a variable or attribute are re-raised with an added note that identifies which variable or attribute was being encoded.
acceptance_criteria: When a writable backend encodes a variable with an available variable name, the backend should preserve that name when delegating to its string or variable encoder instead of dropping it.
When string or char-array encoding emits a warning or raises an error for a specific variable, the resulting user-visible context should identify that variable rather than being anonymous.

When variable encoding fails during store encoding, the raised exception should include a note naming the variable and its value; when attribute encoding fails, the raised exception should include analogous attribute context.
When `encode_variable` is used without a `name`, serialization should still proceed with existing behavior.
